review_notes: I read the whole target file. I compared its blocks with the sibling odd-core proofs in OddCoreScalar, OddCoreTransvection, OddCoreRank, and the grep hits in AltOddCore, OddCoreHeis, SurvivorLineRankY, OneSmallSPLIbU3Rank, MonomialWeightsOne and SevenOnThree. I read fully only the first three of those siblings; for the rest I checked only the grep line hits for hc, hθfix and hατ. I did not check whether each sibling's hypotheses match exactly, or whether each could import an upstream helper without creating a cycle. The proposed helpers are untested, and the names I give are suggestions. Another way to cut the repetition is a single lemma that returns the whole prelude (D, φ, ψ, hD, hc). I did not work that out.

findings.excerpt:
obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hfix ⟨θ, hθfix⟩
  have hθk : θ ^ s ^ k = 1 := congrArg Subtype.val hk
findings.problem: The target already extracts this argument as a lemma. It says that an elementary abelian p-subgroup A of N(Sg) acting trivially on D lies in C(Sg), when the fixer of D in Aut(Sg) is an s-group and s ≠ p. The same argument is written out inline in at least three other odd-core proofs, with the same steps: θ ∈ fixingSubgroup, then θ^(s^k)=1 and θ^p=1, then gcd, then θ=1, then x*y*x⁻¹=y. Those proofs are OddCoreScalar.stmtOddCoreRankScalar (lines 187-212), OddCoreTransvection (lines 78-101) and OddCoreRank.stmtOddCoreRank' (lines 148-173). The grep also shows the same hθfix block in AltOddCore, OddCoreHeis, SurvivorLineRankY, OneSmallSPLIbU3Rank and MonomialWeightsOne. The lemma sits in a downstream file that imports OddCoreScalar, so the earlier files cannot use it and each re-proves the argument. A fix to the argument has to be made in many places.
findings.proposed_change: Move le_centralizer_of_fixing, together with map_pow_ne_of_index where it fits, to an upstream module imported by all odd-core files, for example the file that defines the abstract odd-core lemmas (OddCorePiecesD2 or OddCoreRankAux). The lemma takes hAS, hA : IsElemAbelian p A, hfix and hall (A acts trivially on D), and its proof does not change. Each sibling then replaces its block by `exact le_centralizer_of_fixing hs hp hsp hXS hX hfix hall`. In OddCoreScalar this is hψ's `by_contra hall; push Not at hall; exact hnc (…)`. OddCoreTransvection uses the single-element version (hψ : ψ ζA ≠ 1), so it needs either a variant for one element ζ of A or a pointwise form of the lemma. Both fit the same proof.
findings.benefit: The roughly 25-line argument is stated and proved once. The 5-10 sibling proofs shrink and each hψ step becomes a one-line call. Any change to the fixing-subgroup argument is then made in one place.

findings.excerpt:
have hc : commutator D ≤ Subgroup.center D := by
    rw [_root_.commutator_def]
    refine Subgroup.commutator_le.mpr fun x _ y _ => ?_
    refine Subgroup.mem_center_iff.mpr fun z => ?_
findings.problem: This block turns the output of odd_critical_exponent_subgroup, hcl : ⁅D, ⊤⁆ ≤ D ⊓ centralizer D, into commutator D ≤ center D. Every caller of odd_critical_exponent_subgroup that needs class two redoes it. The same block appears in OddCoreScalar (214-220), OddCoreTransvection (103-109), OddCoreRank (175-181), AltOddCore, OddCoreHeis, SurvivorLineRankY, OneSmallSPLIbU3Rank and MonomialWeightsOne. Other files restate it with small variations: P65Coprime (92-103), Linear.lean (318-323) and a private copy in AltSixCoreClassTwo (29-33). Each copy is a separate, slightly different proof of the same fact. It needs `commutator_mem_commutator`, `mem_centralizer_iff`, and a coercion argument in Subtype.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma in CFSG.SectionRank.Ccomm.OddCritical, next to odd_critical_exponent_subgroup. Its statement is: for D : Subgroup P with hcl : ⁅D, (⊤ : Subgroup P)⁆ ≤ D ⊓ Subgroup.centralizer (D : Set P), conclude commutator D ≤ Subgroup.center D. The proof is the existing 6-line block: commutator_def, commutator_le, mem_center_iff, then Subtype.ext applied to mem_centralizer_iff.mp (hcl (commutator_mem_commutator x.2 (mem_top _))).2. At line 94 the target replaces the block with `have hc := commutator_le_center_of_critical hcl`, and OddCoreScalar etc. do the same. Alternatively, odd_critical_exponent_subgroup could return the class-two statement directly.
findings.benefit: About 10 lines of coercion-heavy proof are removed from each of more than a dozen call sites. The proof is written once. A reader sees `hc` as a named consequence of criticality and does not have to read the unfolding.

findings.excerpt: have hατ : ∀ x : A, φ ⟨t, htS⟩ * ψ x = ψ (α x) * φ ⟨t, htS⟩ := fun x => by
findings.problem: The proof shows that φ(t)·ψ(x) = ψ(t x t⁻¹)·φ(t), where ψ is φ restricted to the abelian subgroup A and α is conjugation by t. It does this by unfolding the two homomorphisms, rewriting with ← map_mul twice, applying congr 1 and Subtype.ext, and finishing with `group`. The proof is the same in OddCoreScalar (179-186), OddCoreTransvection (70-77), OddCoreRank (140-147), AltOddCore (154), and OddCoreHeis (174). Each copy repeats the unfolding and `change`, so the lines are noisy. The general fact is unrelated to the scalar situation: for any φ : N(Sg) →* H, any A ≤ N(Sg), and any t in both N(Sg) and N(A), φ conjugates the A-action by t.
findings.proposed_change: State once, upstream of all these files: for hAS : A ≤ normalizer Sg, htS : t ∈ normalizer Sg, htA : t ∈ normalizer A and φ : normalizer Sg →* H, we have ∀ x : A, φ ⟨t,htS⟩ * φ (Subgroup.inclusion hAS x) = φ (Subgroup.inclusion hAS (A.normalizerMonoidHom ⟨t,htA⟩ x)) * φ ⟨t,htS⟩. The proof is the existing `rw [← map_mul, ← map_mul]; congr 1; apply Subtype.ext; change …; group`. Each user then writes `have hατ := conj_intertwine hAS htS htA φ`. The definition of ψ as φ.comp (inclusion hAS) already makes the two statements definitionally equal, so the call should typecheck up to unfolding.
findings.benefit: This removes the `change` boilerplate and the unfolding, which are fragile if the definitions of `normalizerMonoidHom` or `inclusion` change. The shared lemma shows that the point is an equivariance statement.
